page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8i.3xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 8475B processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.7 GHz. It allocates 12 dedicated vCPUs along with 48.0 GB of system memory, providing a uniform ratio of 4.0 GB of memory per core. This symmetric resource distribution maintains equal computational and memory headroom for standard workloads.

Hardware infrastructure for this instance excludes local storage disks and discrete graphics processing units. All persistent storage operations rely entirely on remote cloud storage options. Network performance is provisioned with a 10 Gbps baseline bandwidth, and the server includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses by default. The omission of local NVMe storage and GPU accelerators keeps the footprint focused strictly on standard general-purpose computing needs.

The 1:4 vCPU-to-memory architecture provides steady resource efficiency without allocating underutilized hardware features. The instance is suited for multi-tier web hosting, application backends, distributed microservices, CI/CD pipeline workers, and moderate database services that do not necessitate local NVMe caching.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g8i.3xlarge is a general-purpose instance deployed on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8475B processor running at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 12 dedicated vCPUs paired with 48.0 GB of system memory, establishing a standard 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The server has no integrated local storage or discrete graphics accelerators, requiring remote block storage for operational disk access. Network capabilities are defined by a 10 Gbps baseline bandwidth. By avoiding specialized hardware accelerators or attached local drives, the configuration emphasizes predictable compute and memory density. It is well matched for enterprise web applications, microservices, container hosts, and moderate transactional databases requiring dedicated compute threads.
